_meta.title: CONTROL-PLANE-GENERALIZATION-001 Task Contract (G1)
_meta.purpose: Generalized task contract for the isolated Control Plane pilot family (task_id prefix CONTROL-PLANE-PILOT-). This is a NEW, additive file -- it does NOT modify .automation/tasks/schema.json (Approved under ADR-022 Section 13), and existing task files/consumers are unaffected.
_meta.does_not_extend: .automation/tasks/schema.json v1.2.0 (Approved, ADR-022). Any future decision to fold these fields into the Approved schema requires a separate ADR Amendment -- out of scope for this generalization task.
_meta.convention: Follows the same style as .automation/tasks/schema.json: an annotated example task, validated by the gateway's Code node (manual field checks in JS), not a strict JSON-Schema $ref validator -- consistent with existing project convention.

field_contract.task_id: string, required. MUST start with 'CONTROL-PLANE-PILOT-' for this pilot family -- this string prefix IS the namespace boundary enforced at both gateway and executor.
field_contract.parent_task_id: string|null. Links a task to the governance decision that authorized it (e.g. the CUE decision record task_id).
field_contract.depends_on: array of task_id strings, required (may be empty). AUTONOMOUS-NIGHT-SHIFT-001 G7: the executor will not process this task until every task_id listed here has automation.state == COMPLETED. A dependency on a nonexistent or non-COMPLETED task_id blocks (fail-closed).
field_contract.task_type: string, required. MUST be a member of the executor's ALLOWED_TASK_TYPES allowlist (currently: ['pilot_echo'] only). Any other value is rejected at the gateway (VALIDATION_FAILED) before it ever reaches the executor -- this is the G3/G8 isolation mechanism, not a convention the executor merely promises to respect.
field_contract.scope.namespace: string, required. MUST equal 'control-plane-pilot'. Any other value is rejected -- this is the task-namespace / production-namespace separation boundary (G3/G8).
field_contract.scope.allowed_paths: array, required (may be empty). Reserved for future task_types that touch the filesystem; task_type=pilot_echo touches no paths at all, so this stays empty. The executor MUST reject any task_type declaring a non-empty allowed_paths until a future generalization task explicitly authorizes it.
field_contract.authorized_by: string, required, non-empty. Who/what authorized this task's creation (a person's name, or 'CUE' for a CUE-issued pilot task). Not a cryptographic signature -- an audit-trail field, consistent with this repo's existing evidence conventions.
field_contract.authorized_by_task_order: string, required, non-empty (CORPUS-FACTORY-INTEGRATION-PILOT-001, ADR-026 Section 2.4). Names the specific Task Order or ADR that authorized this task -- distinct from authorized_by (which names the person/agent). Only required for corpus-factory-pilot namespace tasks; control-plane-pilot tasks predate this field and remain valid without it.
field_contract.production_mutation: boolean, required. MUST be false for every task in this namespace. A task declaring true is rejected at the gateway (VALIDATION_FAILED) -- there is no code path in this generalization that permits true to proceed.
field_contract.required_evidence: array of strings, required. Names of evidence artifacts the executor MUST produce for a task_type. Used only as a documentation/checklist field in this pilot -- not yet enforced by code (would require a post-hoc evidence-completeness checker, explicitly out of scope for this task per the prohibition list; a future generalization task could add it).
field_contract.constraints.max_runtime_s: number, required. Upper bound the executor should honor for subprocess timeouts.
field_contract.constraints.allow_production_paths: boolean, required. MUST be false. Present so a future task_type cannot silently default into touching production paths -- the field must exist and be explicitly false.
